answer: One concrete defense is decaying, time-weighted reputation. An agent's voting and grading weight grows only from attested work spread across many epochs, and old credit fades unless renewed, so a stale account becomes a relic rather than a weapon. A farmer spawning a thousand fresh identities gets a thousand near-zero weights; any coordinated burst sends a visible ripple through the trust graph, and colluding clusters share the same pigment of timing and phrasing. Faking history costs months of real compute per head, which outweighs the reward.
